rules.fact: Title boundary polygons show the position and indicative extent of a registered property.
Direct live dataset readback reports 2,792,111 title-boundary entities.
Direct live dataset readback reports collector last ran on 2026-07-27.
Direct live dataset readback reports new data last found on 2026-07-23.
Dataset origin notes some MHCLG-created data is being replaced with authoritative sources.
Dataset is licensed under Open Government Licence v3.0.
Dataset carries 2026 HM Land Registry Crown copyright/database-rights attribution.
Polygon geometry carries 2026 Ordnance Survey Crown copyright/database-rights attribution.
Coordinate API queries return entities whose geometry intersects the supplied point.
Coordinate API permits multiple dataset parameters and returns entities from any that cover the point.
For registered properties, UPRN passed via q is described as more precise than a coordinate.
Entity responses include fields such as name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point.
Custom geometry coordinates should use WGS84 / EPSG:4326.
The API has no batch endpoint for portfolio screening.
Portfolio screening should issue one request per property.
Bulk downloads are available in CSV, JSON and where applicable GeoJSON and Parquet.
Search-entity response extension must be json, html or geojson.
Longitude and latitude point filters require each other.
INSPIRE Index Polygons contain locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are a subset of HM Land Registry's Index Polygons database for freehold land and property.
INSPIRE data is divided into separate files for each local-authority area.
A polygon crossing a local-authority boundary can appear in both local-authority files.
Each INSPIRE Index Polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID related to a registered title.
HM Land Registry says an INSPIRE ID can be used with Find a Property to obtain title registration and plan.
Registered-title extent cannot be established from INSPIRE polygons alone; the individual title plan is required.
A single title number may contain several polygons, each with a separate Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
Absence of an INSPIRE ID may mean unregistered land or a leasehold/other tenure excluded from INSPIRE.
INSPIRE polygons and attributes are reusable under the Open Government Licence.
Reuse requires HM Land Registry source attribution.
Reuse of polygon geometry also requires Ordnance Survey attribution.
The INSPIRE dataset updates on the first Sunday of each month.
A monthly INSPIRE release shows data from the previous month.
INSPIRE files are published as GML.
HM Land Registry polygon coordinates are captured against the British National Grid.
HM Land Registry warns BNG-to-WGS84 reprojection can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
The public download index lists both London Borough of Barnet and London Borough of Enfield with GML downloads.
Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m covers approximately 99% of England.
The 1m DTM is produced from last/only returns with surface objects removed to model terrain.
The 1m composite was produced in 2022.
The 1m composite combines the Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest best-resolution data is preferred.
Resampled data used bilinear interpolation before merging.
The 2022 composite includes surveys from 2000-06-06 through 2022-04-02.
The 1m data is downloadable as GeoTIFF rasters.
The GeoTIFF data is supplied in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevation values are in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
The 1m composite uses the OSTN15 transformation method.
Individual surveys contributing to the composite had vertical accuracy of +/-15cm RMSE.
The 1m composite is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
The 1m composite CRS is EPSG:27700.
The persistent WCS endpoint is named lidar-composite-digital-terrain-model-dtm-1m/wcs.
Environment Agency WCS elevation services use OGC WCS version 2.0.1.
WCS is documented as providing raw pixel elevation data.
WMS is documented as showing a summarised version of the elevation data.
WCS GeoTIFF NoData is represented by -3.4028235e+38.
The LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud metadata reports quarterly update frequency.
OS Terrain 50 is an open height dataset and digital terrain model product for Great Britain.
OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July.
Grid and contour data are supplied in 10km-by-10km tiles.
Terrain 50 tiles are identified from the National Grid reference of the tile south-west corner.
The Terrain 50 grid has regular 50m post spacing.
Terrain 50 contours use a 10m contour interval.
OS Terrain 50 is Open Data and is free for commercial, educational and personal use.
Terrain 50 grid data is available in ASCII grid and GML.
Terrain 50 contour formats include GML, Esri Shapefile, GeoPackage and vector tiles.
Terrain 50 online download is available with no registration required.
The tiled national supply contains 2,858 tiles.
Those tiles are arranged into 55 folders representing 100km grid squares.
Terrain 50 provides full national coverage of Great Britain.
A full national Terrain 50 grid-tile supply is about 157 MB compressed.
Terrain 50 is designed for annual full-tile resupply.
ASCII grid rows contain 200 pixels.
Each ASCII grid pixel is 50m by 50m.
Terrain 50 ASCII height values are given to the nearest 0.1m.
OS OpenData parts of the Downloads API do not require an API key.
The OS Downloads API does not provide access to previous OpenData releases.
